title: The One Teaching of Jesus That Many Christians Avoid
paragraphs: The One Teaching of Jesus That Many Christians Avoid
Verses they post under sunsets, coffee cups, and worship music.
“I can do all things through Christ.”
“For I know the plans I have for you.”
But there is one teaching of Jesus many believers quietly step around.
Not because they do not know it exists.
But because if taken seriously… it changes everything.
It confronts the version of faith that wants heaven without surrender.
And Jesus did not whisper it once.
He repeated it over and over again.
Almost like He knew future generations would try to avoid it.
The word “ἀπαρνέομαι” (aparneomai) does not mean slight inconvenience.
The same root language is used when Peter denied knowing Jesus.
Jesus was not calling people to merely improve themselves.
He was calling them to deny the throne of self.
And this is where many Christians grow uncomfortable.
Because modern culture teaches self-exaltation while Jesus teaches self-crucifixion.
“The heart is deceitful above all things.”
Many people want a Jesus who comforts.
Few want the Jesus who confronts.
Yet both are the same Christ.
And the One who overturns tables.
Somewhere along the way, parts of Christianity became centered around avoiding discomfort instead of carrying crosses.
But Jesus never hid the cost of discipleship.
In Luke 9:23, the original Greek carries tremendous force:
“εἴ τις θέλει ὀπίσω μου ἔρχεσθαι, ἀπαρνησάσθω ἑαυτὸν καὶ ἀράτω τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ καθ’ ἡμέραν.”
“If anyone desires to come after Me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily.”
Every hidden battle nobody else sees.
Every moment your flesh wants the throne again.
That is where Christianity becomes real.
Not in how many Bible verses fit your Instagram bio.
Real Christianity begins where self dies.
And this is why so many avoid this teaching.
Because denial of self feels like death.
Paul was not advertising a comfortable religion.
The death of the false self that demanded control.
But here is the paradox many miss.
The death Jesus calls us into is the doorway to actual life.
Because the self we desperately protect is often the very prison destroying us.
The exhausting pressure to appear okay.
Some people are not tired because life is hard.
They are tired because carrying a false version of themselves is crushing their soul.
This is why Jesus offended religious people so often.
Because religious performance without surrender is still rebellion.
In Hebrew thought, the heart was not merely emotion.
When God wanted someone’s heart, He was not asking for partial emotion.
He was demanding the center throne.
And many Christians today give Jesus attendance without surrender.
A public image of holiness while private compromise quietly grows underground.
Jesus never came merely to improve behavior.
He came to resurrect dead souls.
And resurrection only comes after death.
That is the part many avoid.
Yet Jesus continually invited people into costly obedience.
When the rich young ruler approached Him in Matthew 19, Jesus exposed the idol hidden beneath morality.
But not at the cost of his god.
Love without truth is not biblical love.
Truth without love is not biblical truth.
This is why His words still cut through generations.
Hebrews 4:12 says the Word of God is:
The Greek word used for sword there is:
A blade designed not merely to wound.
And sometimes Scripture hurts before it heals.
Because infection must be exposed before restoration can begin.
Some of the deepest spiritual moments happen when God confronts the thing we hoped He would ignore.
Jesus does not expose to destroy.
That word has become uncomfortable in modern Christianity.
Because surrender means Jesus is actually Lord.
In the earliest Christian confession, believers declared:
In the Roman world, saying “Caesar is Lord” was politically expected.
So proclaiming Jesus as Lord was not casual religious language.
Modern Christianity often celebrates Jesus as Savior while resisting Him as Lord.
But biblically, you cannot separate the two.
The same Jesus who forgives sin also commands repentance.
The same Jesus who heals also calls people to holiness.
The same Jesus who welcomes sinners also says:
And maybe this is why many avoid His teaching.
But the terrifying beauty of the Gospel is this:
Whatever you lose for Christ was never greater than what you gain in Him.
People who truly surrender to Jesus often discover something shocking.
The freedom they searched for in sin was actually found in obedience.
Not because Christianity is about rules.
The Greek word for sin, “ἁμαρτία” (hamartia), originally carried the idea of missing the mark.
Falling short of God’s holy design.
Sin is not merely breaking arbitrary rules.
It is separation from the life we were created for.
And every human being feels that fracture.
But nothing heals separation from God except reconciliation through Jesus Christ.
The kind that cost Heaven everything.
In Aramaic, one of the words connected to grace is “ṭaybūṯā” (ܛܲܝܒܘܼܬܵܐ).
It carries the idea of lovingkindness,
undeserved favor flowing from the character of God.
This is why the Gospel is simultaneously offensive and beautiful.
Because it tells humanity two truths at once.
You are more sinful than you realized.
And more loved than you imagined.
Jesus did not die because sin was small.
He died because sin was catastrophic.
And He did not stay in the grave.
The empty tomb became Heaven’s declaration that death itself had been defeated.
And still transforming lives right now.
Especially the person reading this who feels too far gone.
Somebody reading this has spent years pretending.
You smile publicly while quietly collapsing internally.
You know how to look spiritually alive.
But deep down, your soul feels numb.
And maybe nobody else sees it.
And unbelievably… He still wants you.
The version terrified of being fully known.
And still stretches out nail-scarred hands.
This is why the Gospel remains undefeated.
Because no amount of darkness can outmatch the mercy of Christ.
But mercy does not mean permission to stay unchanged.
The Christian life is not sinless perfection.
And yes, sometimes that process hurts.
Because God loves us too much to leave us enslaved to the things destroying us.
A loving surgeon cuts to heal.
A loving Savior confronts to restore.
That is the teaching many Christians avoid.
The Gospel is not merely an invitation to believe facts about Jesus.
It is a summons to die and be reborn.
To leave the kingdom of self.
And enter the Kingdom of God.
Because Jesus did not carry a cross so we could casually wear one as jewelry while ignoring His commands.
He carried it to rescue us from sin,
Maybe that is why His teaching still unsettles hearts two thousand years later.
Because somewhere deep inside, people know He is telling the truth.
If that is you, do not ignore this moment.
The conviction you feel may be the mercy of God pulling you back before your heart hardens further.
But He never promised discipleship without surrender.
This hit harder than you expected.
One day, every hidden thing will stand before a holy God.
